title: Long-Standing Service Customers: Hold Extension Days on Vehicle Purchase Agreements
content:
A long-standing service customer is held longer when a hold on a reserved deal under the Vehicle Purchase Agreements is extended. Tenure is read from the opening date of the buyer's active service account in **Service Accounts and Repair Orders**.

**Tenure clause.**
- The buyer's active service account was opened **at least 120 whole months** before the handling date: **2 days** are added to the extension length.
- It was opened **at least 60 but fewer than 120 whole months** before: **1 day** is added.
- Otherwise no tenure days are added. This covers a newer account, an account not in active status, and a buyer without a service account.

**Counting whole months.** Whole months run from the account's opening date to the handling date. A month is whole once the same day of the month is reached.

| Whole months from opening to the handling date (active account) | Tenure days added |
|---|---|
| 120 or more | 2 |
| 60 to 119 | 1 |
| 59 or fewer | None |

**Boundary cases (hypothetical dates).**
- An account opened on the 20th of a month reaches 120 whole months on the 20th of the same month ten years later. A handling date on that day gives 2 days, and a handling date one day earlier (119 whole months) gives 1 day.
- An account opened on the 20th reaches 60 whole months on the 20th five years later. On that day 1 day is added, and the day before, none.
- An account opened twelve years ago but now closed adds nothing, because it is not an active account.
